title: Orthogonal separation of independent Gaussian polynomial statistics
decision_reason: Exact formulation, independent current restatement, theorem-scope checks and separated A29 self-pass passed; no matching unresolved resolution claim located.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: Two nonconstant real polynomials evaluated at one standard Gaussian vector.
problem_fingerprint.dimension: Every finite n≥2; n=2 is known.
problem_fingerprint.regularity_and_data_class: Arbitrary finite polynomial degrees and real coefficients; no evenness, convexity or chaos restriction.
problem_fingerprint.parameter_range: All pairs whose outputs are independent.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: For every n and such pair, there exist a single orthogonal O, a split 1≤k<n and two polynomials on the disjoint blocks.
problem_fingerprint.normalization: X has mean zero and covariance I_n.
problem_fingerprint.observable_or_norm: Independence of distributions, defined on all Borel rectangles.
problem_fingerprint.requested_conclusion: After composition with O, both polynomials depend on disjoint coordinate blocks, pointwise on R^n.
problem_fingerprint.computational_model_and_dependencies: Existence statement, no algorithm, approximate independence or unproved dependency.

statement_source_and_scope_match: HH22 §1 gives the standard-Gaussian formulation and n=2 exception; MNPP16 §1.5 defines the disjoint-coordinate split. Removing constant statistics only omits trivial endpoint cases. LOS26 §1 explicitly specifies a standard Gaussian.
proposed_statement_text: Must every independent pair of nonconstant real polynomial statistics of a standard Gaussian vector separate into disjoint coordinate blocks after an orthogonal transformation?
applied_significance: Foundational characterization of independence of polynomial summaries of Gaussian observations. The interpretation as separating orthogonal sources of variation follows directly from the statement; no finite-sample inference guarantee is claimed.

later_results_and_resolution_checks.assessment_and_remaining_gap: Arbitrary real polynomials need not have symmetric convex sublevel sets.

hypothesis_comparison: Both functions convex; one analytic and globally minimized at zero.
later_results_and_resolution_checks.assessment_and_remaining_gap: Polynomial analyticity alone does not supply convexity or the minimum condition.

hypothesis_comparison: Each statistic is a finite sum of squares, the jth term lying in the jth chaos.
later_results_and_resolution_checks.assessment_and_remaining_gap: Proof separates nonnegative component covariances; arbitrary polynomial expansions do not provide this representation.

hypothesis_comparison: Vector jointly Gaussian; positive absolute-power exponents; equality criterion for its coordinates.
later_results_and_resolution_checks.assessment_and_remaining_gap: Polynomial outputs are generally not jointly Gaussian. No extension to arbitrary independent polynomial functions is supplied; no indirect unlinking implication located.

hypothesis_comparison: Complex coefficients; all pure moments vanish but mixed moments do not.
later_results_and_resolution_checks.assessment_and_remaining_gap: Does not construct an independent pair of real statistics. Indeed the displayed nonzero mixed moments fail the factorization independence would impose.

closest_existing_or_new_entries.distinction: Mutual-information extremization for Boolean inputs through binary noise, not Gaussian polynomial independence.
Balanced measurable Gaussian partitions maximizing noisy agreement, not an orthogonal decomposition theorem.
